en: To live in the fear of God
let him pray to God night and day
that He will give me strength,
I have not spared for you;
have also shown it to you:
chosen a prince of the Empire,
are You, O God my Lord;
That I may yet remain pious,
that wounds me through my heart.
my God, be pleased to keep
that they do not take me by surprise
so I have had to sigh
But God has raised him up,
After the sour I shall receive
from God my Lord the sweet;
that is, that I may die
Nothing moves me more to pity
with the strength of my army,
If it had been the will of the Lord
I would gladly have turned away
But the Lord from up above,
from the bottom of my heart
that He will save my cause,
it will soon be over here.
notes: The first letters of the fifteen stanzas spell WILLEM VAN NASSOV (William of Nassau); the acrostic is lost in translation and could be mentioned on the page.
The source text is in modernized spelling (as on Wikisource), not the 1570s orthography; it was translated as given.

line 1.2: 'Duitsen' (Duytschen) in the 16th century meant 'Dutch' in the old wide sense, of the Low German and Dutch lands, not 'German' in today's sense; William's family was from Nassau in Germany. Both senses are argued; editor should choose how to gloss it.
line 1.7-1.8 and stanza 15: the song presents William as loyal to Philip II and fighting only his ministers (Alba), the official line of the revolt at the time.
line 2.4: 'om land, om luid gebracht' = deprived of land and people ('luid' = people, subjects).
line 2.8: 'regiment' = rule, government (his offices as stadholder), not a military regiment.
line 4.2: 'heb ik u niet verschoond' = I have not spared (withheld) for your sake; it does not mean he did not spare the subjects.
line 4.5: 'is gebleven' = remained (on the field), i.e. fell: Adolf of Nassau, killed at Heiligerlee in 1568.
line 5.3: 'een vorst des rijks verkoren' is unclear: 'chosen' may mean elevated or simply 'a chosen prince of the (Holy Roman) Empire'.
line 6.8: 'die mij mijn hart doorwondt' = that wounds my heart through (pierces me to the heart).
line 9.3-9.4: 'daarna zo doet verlangen mijn vorstelijk gemoed' = for that my princely heart (mind) longs; word order kept.
line 10.4: 'des Konings landen goed' can be read as 'the King's good lands' or 'the King's lands and their goods'.
line 11.3: 'vermeten' = presumptuous, arrogant; the tyrant is the Duke of Alba.
line 11.5: 'bij Maastricht begraven' = entrenched (dug in) near Maastricht, in 1568; not 'buried'.
line 13.1: 'Zeer christlijk was gedreven mijn prinselijk gemoed' = my princely mind (heart) was driven in a very Christian way; rendered loosely in word order.
line 14.1: 'Oorlof' = farewell (literally leave, permission to go).
line 8.2: 'Sauel' is the old form of Saul, kept as the name.
